name: Parsi-Dari
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog: entry duplicates Zoroastrian Dari [gbz]; Ivanow, Vladimir 1935-1939 descriptions of the Gabri/Dari dialect plausibly cover stress; not online

new_statements.quote: The accent is fairly mobile, and, as in many dialects, it does not observe the rule of LP of falling on the end of the word. The local Yazdi form of bazari has its own peculiarity, keeping the accent on the first, instead of the last syllable, which sounds rather odd; though the accent is never sharp. Gabri has the accent on the first syllable only in some verbal forms. The accent seems to consist neither in merely raising the voice, nor in merely prolonging it, but in doing both, in a varying degree, depending on intonation, and, perhaps, on the rate of speech.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Ivanow gives no positional rule: word accent is 'fairly mobile' and does not follow the Literary Persian (LP) final-stress rule; only some verbal forms carry initial accent (the local Persian koine of Yazd, 'bazari', is noted as initial-accenting). Elsewhere in the same grammar the definite suffix -é attracts the accent (p. 60), the aorist prefix e- may be stressed for future emphasis without taking the main accent (p. 78), the Kermani durative prefix i- is stressed in the perfect (p. 83), and the 3sg copula suffix -uné is only semi-accented, the main accent staying on the host word (p. 85). The only other first-hand statement, Toosarvandani & Farudi 2003 p. 26 (Qasemabad, Yazd), says 'stress in Dari is always on the first syllable of a verb' and treats tonic pronouns as separate stress domains; it says nothing about nouns.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Ivanow p. 85: in the 3sg copula suffix -uné 'u is very short, and é is semi-accented (as the real accent rests on the word itself)'. No general secondary-stress statement.
new_statements.exceptions: Definite/correlative suffix -é/-á attracts the accent (pitrügé 'the boy', wazîré; p. 60); the adverbial preverb bar 'out' is 'emphatic, attracting the accent' (p. 70); imperative bi- in biure/biwre 'is sharply accented' (p. 83); 'occasional difference in the accent in the two sub-dialects' Yazdi vs Kermani (p. 54).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level accent in connected speech as heard by Ivanow (fast talkers, no measurements); accent described as a mixture of pitch raising and lengthening 'depending on intonation'. Sub-dialects: Yazdi Gabri (YG) and Kermani Gabri (KG). The 2003 Farudi/Toosarvandani remark concerns verbs and clitic-vs-word tests in the Qasemabad (Yazd) dialect.
new_statements.identity_note: pars1252 'Parsi-Dari' [prd] is a Glottolog Bookkeeping entry that duplicates Zoroastrian Dari [gbz] = zoro1242 ('Zoroastrian Yazdi'; also Behdini, Gabri, Gavruni). Any catalog entry should be filed under zoro1242 and pars1252 marked as its duplicate. Ivanow 1935 describes 'Gabri' with two sub-dialects, Yazdi (YG) and Kermani (KG), and notes occasional accent differences between them; Toosarvandani & Farudi 2003 describe the Qasemabad dialect of Yazd. The Judeo-Yazdi penultimate-stress statement (Gindin, EIr) belongs to a different language and must not be attached here.
